$comment: Every retrieval expectation the connector is held to, in one place. scripts/retrieval-gate.mjs evaluates it; npm run benchmark, npm run calibrate and the core tests all use that one evaluation. The website's own public benchmark stays in data/benchmark.json as the "website" category. See docs/BENCHMARK.md.

website.note: the website's public benchmark: every question in the top three and strong

shorthand.note: at least 23 in the top three and 21 strong. "chiller and BMS end of life in a 90s office" is judged weak: the BMS page answers half of it and no one page carries both.

pinned.note: rankings the protocol and HTTP tests assert outright

outside.note: off-topic questions that share the corpus's words; may never get worse; target zero. The six still judged strong all land on library pages, which are judged on their own passages and exempt from the domain-evidence check.

target.note: questions where the right page exists and another used to win (fire doors, switchboards, concrete cancer, tin roofs, asbestos registers, rusting render, obsolete lifts, painted sprinkler heads, basement water, reading a capital register, balcony concrete). A floor that may only rise.

faq.note: one authored FAQ per library page should find its own page in the top three; 98 of 103 before passage scoring.

typo.note: authored FAQ questions with two letters of one long word swapped, as people type; one slip inside a word is searched as the word it nearly is

verbose.note: authored FAQ questions wrapped in conversation ("Hi, I have a question ... thanks"); the wrapper is dropped from the query
